_comment: Single source of truth for Talon's blog. Edit this file, then run: python tools/build-blog.py && python tools/build-sitemap.py. Never hand-edit anything under /blog/ - the builder overwrites it. Adding a post is an entry in `posts` below; nothing else needs touching.

_field_guide.slug: URL segment. Lowercase, hyphens, no dates. Becomes /blog/<slug>/ and cannot be changed later without breaking links.
_field_guide.title: The headline, as published. Used as the <h1> and in the <title> tag.
_field_guide.date: YYYY-MM-DD. Drives ordering and the published date shown on the page.
_field_guide.date_source: Where the date came from. Say plainly if it is an authoring date rather than a confirmed publication date - this bit Hollie's site once.
_field_guide.tag: One of the values in `tags` below. Shown on the card and used by the archive filter.
_field_guide.area: Optional. A service area from `service_areas` below, when a post is genuinely about that place. Drives the local-SEO half of the blog. Leave empty for general posts - do NOT tag a post with an area it is not really about.
_field_guide.excerpt: 1-2 sentences for the archive card and the meta description. Written, not auto-truncated.
_field_guide.paragraphs: Array of strings, one per paragraph. Plain text; the builder escapes and wraps them.
_field_guide.image: Card image, 3:2, ~800px. Empty string renders the branded placeholder instead.
_field_guide.image_wide: Post banner, 2:1, ~1440px. Empty string renders the placeholder.
_field_guide.image_alt: Describe what the image SHOWS, including any words lettered inside it. Empty alt is only for decoration.

_service_areas_note: From the live GBP service-area list, confirmed 2026-09-01. The site currently names only Penn Valley, Lake Wildwood, Nevada County and the Sierra Foothills - the rest have no on-site presence at all, which is the local-SEO gap the blog is partly here to close. Do not invent an area that is not on this list.
_tags_note: Keep this list short. Every tag becomes a filter button on the archive, and a filter with one post in it is worse than no filter.
_posts_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE. The pipeline was built 2026-09-08 ahead of Kim supplying the articles. With no posts, /blog renders an honest empty state rather than a broken page, and it is NOT linked from the site nav or the sitemap until at least one post exists - see build-blog.py.

posts.title: Welcome to The Journal
posts.date_source: Authoring date, not a confirmed publication date. Update this to the day it actually goes live.
posts.excerpt: Talon Construction Company is starting to write down the answers we give homeowners every week — what a foothill build actually involves, where budgets go wrong, and what we ran into on real projects.
paragraphs: Most of what we know about building in Nevada County was learned on job sites, not in a classroom — on foothill lots, since 1981. This is where we are going to start writing some of it down.

Homeowners ask us the same questions before a project starts. What will this actually cost? How long will it take? Why does that slope change the foundation? Do I need a permit for this? What happens if we find something once the walls are open? Those are good questions, and they deserve better than a rushed answer over the phone.
## What is The Journal?

**The Journal** is Talon Construction Company's working notebook, published. It is where we answer the questions homeowners actually ask us, one at a time, in enough detail to be useful before you have hired anybody.

It is not a news feed and it is not a portfolio. If we do not have something useful to say about a subject, we will wait until we do. A post here should either save you a phone call or tell you what to ask on the next one.
## What will we write about?
Three things, in roughly equal measure.

- **Building in the foothills.** Slopes, access, drainage, lake-area requirements, aging structures, and the weather that shapes all of it — the conditions that make a Nevada County build different from a build on flat ground.
- **Planning and budget.** The part of a project most likely to go wrong, and the easiest to get right early. Scope, allowances, unknowns, and where the money actually goes.
- **The work itself.** What we are building, what we ran into, and how it was solved. Specific projects rather than general advice.
Where a post is about a real project, we will say which one and what the conditions were. A claim about how something performs is worth reading only if you can tell where it came from.
## Who is writing this?

Talon is three people. Jordon O'Hara works in the field, on building knowledge and day-to-day leadership on site. Mike Novo founded the company and holds the license. Erik Oxenbol works on management, and how a project gets organized and run from start to finish. All three work to the standards Mike set, and you will see all three names in what gets written here.

**Talon Construction Company** is a California licensed general contractor working out of Penn Valley. Michael Novo has personally held license CSLB #397350 since January 1981 — not the company, him, for forty-five years.
That license carries four classifications:
- **Class A**, General Engineering Contractor
- **Class B**, General Building Contractor
- **C-12**, Earthwork and Paving Contractors
- **C-42**, Sanitation System Contractor

Together those cover site engineering, the building itself, earthwork and septic. That is close to the range a foothill project tends to ask for. You can check any California contractor's license yourself, including ours, on the [CSLB license lookup](https://www.cslb.ca.gov/onlineservices/checklicenseII/checklicense.aspx). We would rather you did.
## Where does Talon work?

Talon works across Nevada County and into the surrounding foothills: Penn Valley, Lake Wildwood, Lake of the Pines, Grass Valley, Nevada City, Rough and Ready, North San Juan, Colfax, Truckee and Tahoe City.

Those places do not build the same way. A lake-area remodel answers to rules a Grass Valley addition never sees. Truckee carries a snow load and a season that closes early. Where a post applies to one of them in particular, we will say so rather than leave you to guess.
## What should we write about?

If there is something you would like us to cover, call us at (530) 432-3633 or send it through the contact form. A question you have not been able to get a straight answer to is exactly the kind we want. That is a genuine offer — the best posts here will come from questions homeowners actually asked.
The standard we try to hold to here is the same one we bring to a job. Say what is true, explain the decisions, and do not promise what cannot be delivered.
